statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-45571 (GHSA-crhj-59gh-8x96, GO-2026-5336): go-git did not apply upstream Git path checks, so a crafted repository could write into the main or a submodule .git directory during clone, checkout, pull or submodule update. github.com/go-git/go-git/v5 up to 5.19.0 is affected and 5.19.1 is the patched release (https://github.com/go-git/go-git/security/advisories/GHSA-crhj-59gh-8x96, https://github.com/go-git/go-git/releases/tag/v5.19.1). Checked every scout-cli-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository by 2026-11-27: 25 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to 1.30.0-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/docker-scout, a development build of the Docker Scout CLI, which for every version lists the same Go release and module versions as the scout-cli package of that version, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read the Go build information (Go release and module versions) of that program in every published package; both architectures agree for every build. github.com/go-git/go-git/v5 is v5.18.0 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.20.4-r2, v5.19.0 in 1.20.4-r3 to 1.20.4-r4, v5.19.1 in 1.21.0-r0 to 1.23.1-r4, v5.19.2 in 1.23.1-r5 to 1.30.0-r1. So every build before 1.21.0-r0 ships an affected release and 1.21.0-r0 and every later build ship a fixed one; the range follows the module version each build ships.

CVE-2026-45571 (GHSA-crhj-59gh-8x96, GO-2026-5336): go-git did not apply upstream Git path checks, so a crafted repository could write into the main or a submodule .git directory during clone, checkout, pull or submodule update. github.com/go-git/go-git/v5 up to 5.19.0 is affected and 5.19.1 is the patched release (https://github.com/go-git/go-git/security/advisories/GHSA-crhj-59gh-8x96, https://github.com/go-git/go-git/releases/tag/v5.19.1). CVE-2026-45571 (GHSA-crhj-59gh-8x96, GO-2026-5336): in github.com/go-git/go-git/v5 up to 5.19.0, missing path validation lets a crafted repository write outside the checkout target, including into the main repository's or a submodule's .git directory, when it is cloned, checked out or pulled. It is fixed in v5.19.1, whose release notes include https://github.com/go-git/go-git/pull/2100, which adds a path-validating worktreeFilesystem wrapper for the worktree, and https://github.com/go-git/go-git/pull/2082, which validates submodule names: https://github.com/go-git/go-git/security/advisories/GHSA-crhj-59gh-8x96, https://github.com/go-git/go-git/releases/tag/v5.19.1. The Go vulnerability database lists Clone, PlainClone, Worktree.Checkout, Worktree.Pull and the Submodule update functions as affected: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5336. We read every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the checksum in the package index. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 that keeps its symbol table; we read its Go build information, its function table (which lists runtime.main in every binary) and its raw bytes. Every build has the affected functions PlainCloneContext and (*Worktree).Checkout in its function table. The build information lists go-git v5.16.5 in 0.69.1-r0 to 0.69.3-r3, v5.17.1 in 0.69.3-r4 and 0.69.3-r5, v5.18.0 in 0.69.3-r6 to 0.70.0-r1, v5.19.0 in 0.70.0-r2 to 0.70.0-r4, v5.19.1 in 0.70.0-r5 to 0.71.2-r3 and v5.19.2 from 0.73.0-r0. The function table agrees: in 0.70.0-r4 the functions of the top-level go-git package come from go-git v5.19.0 source and none belongs to worktreeFilesystem, and from 0.70.0-r5 they come from v5.19.1 or later and include the worktreeFilesystem methods added by the fix. The range is therefore fixed at 0.70.0-r5.
